BEFORE THE ILLINOIS WORKERS’ COMPENSATION COMMISSION 
 
 
BRUCE BALTHAZOR, 
 
 
Petitioner, 
 
 
vs. 
NO:  19WC025473 
 
 
CLARK DIETRICH BUILDING SYSTEMS, 
 
 
Respondent. 
 
 
DECISION AND OPINION ON REVIEW 
 
 
Timely Petition for Review having been filed by the Petitioner herein and notice given to 
all parties, the Commission, after considering the issues of accident, notice, causal connection, 
temporary total disability and nature and extent, and being advised of the facts and law, affirms 
and adopts, with the following changes, the Decision of the Arbitrator, which is attached hereto 
and made a part hereof.   
 
The Commission notes that Petitioner underwent a right total hip arthroplasty on 
February 14, 2019.  See Rx2-Exhibit, 5/15/19 record, T.601.  In the first full paragraph on page 6 
(unnumbered)1, the references to “Dr. Van Thiel” in the last two sentences are stricken and 
replaced with “Dr. Thiara.”  See T.32-35.  In the paragraph at the bottom of page 7, the 
references to “Roseland” are stricken and replaced with “Rochelle.”  See T.54-57. 
 
At the top of page 8, the words “Independent Medical” are stricken and replaced with 
“Section 12.”  The Commission notes that Petitioner testified he was in Dr. Thangamani’s office 
for 31 minutes and Dr. Thangamani “kept on asking the same question over and over” but never 
performed an examination.  T.67-69.  Petitioner testified that it was Dr. Thangamani, not 
Petitioner, who terminated the examination.  T.70.  Petitioner testified that he did not refuse to 
answer questions and stay for the examination, but that Dr. Thangamani told him he was “free to 
go.”  T.68, 70-71.  Petitioner testified that Dr. Thangamani repeatedly asked him why he waited 
so long to go to the doctor and Petitioner answered, “I thought I pulled a muscle.”  T.72-74.   
 
 
1 Since the Arbitrator’s Decision does not contain page numbers, our citations are to the page number in the .pdf file. 
26IWCC0128

19WC025473 
Page 2 
In the first sentence of the paragraph at the bottom of page 10, we correct the date of Dr. 
Coe’s examination from November 21, 2022 to March 10, 2020.  The Commission clarifies that 
Dr. Coe testified that based on the history provided by Petitioner, the treating records through 
August 2019 and his examination of Petitioner in March 2020, it was his conclusion that 
Petitioner suffered an injury to his right hip that aggravated pre-existent right hip dysplasia (i.e., 
femoroacetabular impingement) causing labral tearing and a loose body with acute and persistent 
right hip pain.  Px1 at 32, T.197.  Dr. Coe opined that, in the course of Petitioner’s recovery after 
having undergone two hip surgeries, he developed a right knee patellofemoral syndrome with 
knee pain caused by postoperative leg weakness and lower back pain related to awkward 
movement and a gait abnormality, with findings at the L3-4 intervertebral disc.  Id. at 33, T.198.  
Dr. Coe testified that Petitioner’s right hip, leg and lower back symptoms are causally related to 
the accident Petitioner described at work on July 31, 2018, and that his medical treatment was all 
reasonable and necessitated by the work accident.  Id. at 33-34, T.198-199.  Dr. Coe opined that 
Petitioner was at maximum medical improvement and had permanent sedentary restrictions.  Id. 
at 34-35, T.199-200. 
The Commission finds that the first mention of an acute event is contained in the August 
8, 2019 record of Dr. Enke, more than a year after Petitioner’s alleged accident.  Rx2-Exhibit, 
T.601.  Dr. Thangamani testified that Dr. Enke’s August 8, 2019 record is the first one to
mention an acute injury.  Rx1 at 21, 29, T.425, 433.  Dr. Coe testified that if all he had were the
medical records prior to August 8, 2019, he could not say that Petitioner’s condition was related
to any kind of accident.  Px1 at 87-88, T.252-53.  Dr. Coe testified that the first reference to an
acute injury, although confusing, was the August 8, 2019 record of Dr. Enke.  Id. at 89-93,
T.254-58.  Dr. Coe testified that this record was consistent with the information he obtained from
Petitioner, on March 10, 2020, about having experienced feeling a pop and experiencing pain on
July 31, 2018.  Id.  However, on the issue of causation and whether Petitioner’s condition was
related to his alleged work injury, Dr. Coe admitted that none of the treating physicians
addressed that issue.  Id. at 95-96, T.260-61.
All else is affirmed and adopted. 
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that the Decision of the 
Arbitrator filed July 14, 2025 is hereby affirmed and adopted with the changes noted above. 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that the Respondent shall have 
credit for all amounts paid, if any, to or on behalf of the Petitioner on account of said accidental 
injury. 
The party commencing the proceedings for review in the Circuit Court shall file with the 
Commission a Notice of Intent to File for Review in Circuit Court.

An Application for Adjustment of Claim was filed in this matter, and a Notice of Hearing was mailed to each 
party.  The matter was heard by the Honorable Paul Seal, Arbitrator of the Commission, in the city of 
Geneva and Wheaton on February 27, 2025; April 22, 2025.  After reviewing all of the evidence 
presented, the Arbitrator hereby makes findings on the disputed issues checked below and attaches those 
findings to this document.  
DISPUTED ISSUES 
A. 
 Was Respondent operating under and subject to the Illinois Workers' Compensation or Occupational  
Diseases Act? 
B. 
 Was there an employee-employer relationship? 
C. 
 Did an accident occur that arose out of and in the course of Petitioner's employment by Respondent? 
D. 
 What was the date of the accident? 
E. 
 Was timely notice of the accident given to Respondent? 
F. 
 Is Petitioner's current condition of ill-being causally related to the injury? 
G. 
 What were Petitioner's earnings? 
H. 
 What was Petitioner's age at the time of the accident? 
I. 
 What was Petitioner's marital status at the time of the accident? 
J. 
 Were the medical services that were provided to Petitioner reasonable and necessary?  Has Respondent 
 paid all appropriate charges for all reasonable and necessary medical services? 
K. 
 What temporary benefits are in dispute?   
 TPD  
 Maintenance 
 TTD 
L. 
 What is the nature and extent of the injury?  
M. 
 Should penalties or fees be imposed upon Respondent? 
N. 
 Is Respondent due any credit? 
O. 
 Other     
ICArbDec  4/22    
 Web site:  www.iwcc.il.gov 
26IWCC0128

FINDINGS 
On July 31, 2018, Respondent was operating under and subject to the provisions of the Act.   
On this date, an employee-employer relationship did exist between Petitioner and Respondent.   
On this date, Petitioner did not sustain an accident that arose out of and in the course of employment. 
Timely notice of this accident was not given to Respondent. 
Petitioner's current condition of ill-being is not causally related to the accident. 
In the year preceding the injury, Petitioner earned $38,064.00; the average weekly wage was $732.00. 
On the date of accident, Petitioner was 50 years of age, single with 0 dependent children. 
Petitioner has received all reasonable and necessary medical services.   
Respondent has paid all appropriate charges for all reasonable and necessary medical services. 
Respondent shall be given a credit of $0.00 for TTD, $0.00 for TPD, $0.00 for maintenance, and $0.00 for 
other benefits, for a total credit of $See Arbitration Decision. 
Respondent is entitled to a credit of $See below under Section 8(j) of the Act. 
ORDER 
The Arbitrator finds that Petitioner failed to bear his burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that 
he suffered an accident that arose out of and in the course of his employment with the respondent. 
The Arbitrator finds that Petitioner failed to provide evidence that timely notice of accident was provided to 
Respondent. 
The Arbitrator finds that Petitioner failed to bear his burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that 
his current condition of ill-being is causally related to an accident arising out of and in the course of his 
employment with the respondent. 
The Arbitrator finds that the petitioner failed to bear his burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence 
that Respondent is liable for any reasonable, necessary, related medical. 
The Arbitrator finds that the petitioner failed to bear his burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence 
that Respondent is liable for any temporary total disability compensation benefits. 
The Arbitrator finds that the petitioner failed to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that he sustained any 
disability as a result of any accident arising out of and in the course of his employment with the Respondent. 
Compensation is hereby denied. 
RULES REGARDING APPEALS  Unless a party files a Petition for Review within 30 days after receipt of this 
decision, and perfects a review in accordance with the Act and Rules, then this decision shall be entered as the 
decision of the Commission.   
26IWCC0128

however, if an employee's appeal results in either no change or a decrease in this award, interest shall not

STATEMENT OF FACTS 
 
Petitioner testified that in August of 2016, he was employed by Clark Dietrich Building 
Systems. Petitioner testified that he was trained on a mill. On or about July 31, 2018, he was 
operating mill 315 which is a structural cold role formed steel mill. He was doing extremely large, 
heavy studs that morning. They were 50 feet long approximately, 400 or 500 pounds apiece. (AT 
16) Two people maneuvered the heavy studs. He went to slide the heavy stud and is not sure if his 
helper inadvertently dropped his side of the stud. He felt shockwaves come through and a pop in 
his right hip. The Clark leader was Juan Roman. Juan brought Petitioner to Petitioner’s 
supervisor’s office, Daryl Tappler. Daryl and Petitioner wrote out a handwritten statement as to 
what happened. He was taken off the mill for that day. He believes he went home early that day. 
(AT 17)  He went home and used ice and rested. He worked like this for a while, every day he 
would go home pretty sore. After a while, it would not heal, therefore, he scheduled an appointment 
with Ortho Illinois, Dr. Barb who was an Orthopedic doctor. When he knew what was happening 
for sure, he informed     HR    Lynn   Ulrich. (AT 18) Lynn told Petitioner to put it under short-
term disability, that he couldn't do it under Workmen's Comp. Petitioner testified “So mistake I 
made when I went to the doctor, I told them I didn’t know what happened. Basically, I lied to the 
doctor.”  (AT 19)  He did not give a history of anything that happened at work.  From there, they 
recommended I had a labral tear and they recommended I seek treatment with Dr. Van Thiel. (AT 
19)  Petitioner was told the only option was a complete total hip replacement. His first surgery was 
done with Dr. Van Thiel on October 31, 2018. He had some complications with his knee, his leg 
wasn't as strong. He was having problems with his back. He then received an MRI of the back. 
(AT 20) He then consulted with an attorney because he started having anxiety and issues with 
finances. (AT 21) He subpoenaed employment records. He believes the employment records were 
not complete. They were unsigned, no statement from Petitioner. (AT 23) He received physical 
26IWCC0128

therapy. He is in tremendous pain. (AT 24)  He did physical therapy and home therapy to the point 
where he's able to walk without a cane. He is no longer receiving medical treatment. His last 
treatment was a couple of years ago. (AT 26) He testified that he put all his medical treatment 
through group coverage. (AT 27) 
 
He testified that he had health insurance with Clark Dietrich and submitted his bills through 
his group insurance. There were bills paid through Blue Cross Blue Shield and marketplace for a 
while and then through Medicare. (AT 28) At some point, Medicare started paying some of his 
medical bills. After he stopped working for Clark Dietrich, medical bills continued to be paid 
through Clark Dietrich group insurance, Blue Cross Blue Shield for approximately 10 months. 
(AT 29) Petitioner testified that he discharged his attorneys. It was a mutual agreement. Since he 
discharged his attorneys, he has not sent any medical records or medical bills to Respondent. 
Petitioner is not certain what his prior attorney sent to Respondent. (AT 30) He testified that he 
filed a ARDC  against his prior attorneys, Tracy Jones and Stephanie Siebold. (AT 31)  Since he 
discharged Black & Jones, he has talked to two or three large law firms. (AT 32) He filed a 
Complaint against Respondent’s IME Dr. Thangamani because he would not treat Petitioner. He 
filed a Complaint with the hospital. Petitioner then testified he did not file a complaint against Dr. 
Thangamani, he was going to. (AT 33) Petitioner thought the doctor that was being referenced was 
his primary care doctor, Dr. Van Thiel. Dr. Van Thiel was mad at Petitioner because he didn’t 
know anything, he was foreign speaking, hard to understand, not very knowledgeable. (AT 34) 
 
He attended an Independent Medical Examination with Dr. Thangamani and Dr. Jeffrey 
Coe. He does not recall discussing with Dr. Coe that he has hip dysplasia, right hip symptoms, a 
congenital problem that he was born with, genetically determined. (AT 36-38)  He testified that he 
26IWCC0128

never had any prior medical treatment for his hip. (AT 38) He recalled he was diagnosed with a 
congenital or early developmental anatomic structural abnormality by Dr. Barba. (AT 39) He does 
not recall telling Dr. Coe that he had prior right hip symptoms. (AT 41)  He testified that he told 
Dr. Coe that he had prior low back pain, prior chiropractic care. Petitioner has always done 
physical labor jobs. (AT 42) He does not recall that when he was examined by Dr. Coe on March 
10, 2020, that Dr. Coe felt he was at maximum medical improvement. (AT 44) Dr. Coe never told 
Petitioner that he did not injure his right knee, right leg or his back on July 31st. (AT 48) Petitioner 
denies having any discussions with Dr. Coe that has a diagnosis of hip dysplasia, congenital 
condition, something that is genetically determined, that he was either born with or developed in 
childhood. He denies discussing with Dr. Coe that his medical condition was clearly a pre-existing 
condition that pre-existed his accident of July 2018. (AT 48-50)  Petitioner does not recall telling 
Dr. Barba that he reported right hip pain on and off for 13 years, no known injury. (AT 53) He 
testified that Dr. Van Thiel’s report dated October 15, 2018 states mechanism of injury, patient 
reports right hip pain on and off for 13 years, no known injury, because medical records are shared 
between Dr. Van Thiel and Dr. Barba. (AT 54) 
 
Petitioner also received medical treatment at Roseland Community Hospital. He believes 
the medical report from Roseland dated November 5, 2018, stating he was born with hip dysplasia 
and had had difficulties with his hip all his life, is based off the medical record that Dr. Barba and 
Dr. Van Thiel sent to Roseland Community Hospital. He did not fill anything out. (AT 55) He 
does recall providing Roseland Community Hospital with a history that for several years, he has 
been unable to do his hobbies of hunting and fishing, but he hopes to get back to doing this after 
rehabilitation. (AT 57-59) Petitioner testified that the first doctor he provided notice to about a 
work injury may have been Dr. Ryan Enke, or possibly Petitioner’s IME with Dr. Jeffrey Coe. 
26IWCC0128

Petitioner was examined by Dr. Enke on August 8, 2019, stating Petitioner complained of low 
back pain, date of onset, July 2018, mechanism of injury, gradual onset with no known injury. (AT 
60-63) Petitioner was examined by Dr. Thangamani for Respondent’s Independent Medical 
Examination. (AT 67) 
 
Petitioner called Traci Siebler to the stand to testify. Petitioner and Traci have been dating 
for nine years, and are currently engaged. They started living together in August 2017. She testified 
that before Petitioner’s injury, he worked his butt off. He wouldn't stop. After the injury happened, 
he pushed through, refused to go to the doctor, thought it was a pulled muscle or something. Finally 
he couldn’t keep going to work everyday, and went to see a doctor. Petitioner came to find out it 
was a worker’s comp injury. (AT 89)  His abilities are limited now, his life is completely changed. 
(AT 90)  She testified that she attended all of his treating doctors’ office visit and would talk to 
Petitioner about his visits. When Petitioner saw his doctors, he told his doctors about his injury. 
To the best of her knowledge, when Petitioner went to see his treating doctors he would give them 
an exact history of what happened when he was working at Clark. Every time he went to his doctor, 
he would tell his doctor what his complaints were any problems he had and would provide a history 
of what occurred at Clark. (AT 92-94) 
 
Lynn Ulrich testified that she was the senior HR business partner at Clark Dietrich. She 
has had that title for seven years. She is familiar with Petitioner. Petitioner was a manufacturing 
team member. He stopped working for Clark approximately October 19, 2018. (AT 95, 96) Lynn 
did not have any conversations with Petitioner between July 31, 2018 and October 19, 2018, the 
date Petitioner stopped working, regarding a work accident. (AT 98) Lynn testified that at no time 
did she speak with Bruce between July 31, 2018 and October 19th regarding a work comp claim, 
26IWCC0128

since there was no work comp accident. (AT 99) If there was a work comp claim, it would have 
been brought to Lynn’s attention immediately. Petitioner did not report a work comp claim, to a 
supervisor or plant manager as they would have reported it to Lynn. His supervisor was Darryl 
Tappler. The first notice that Lynn received regarding a work comp claim was receipt of 
Petitioner’s Application for Adjustment of Claim sent to Clark. (AT 100)  The first notice received 
was receipt of the Application, in August of 2019, the following year. (AT 101)  After Lynn 
received the Application for Adjustment of Claim, she spoke with Petitioner supervisor, Daryl 
Tappler. Daryl Tappler reported to Lynn that he did not receive any notice of an alleged work 
injury. (AT 103, 104) Lynn also spoke to Daryl Tappler on Friday, February 21, 2025. At such 
time, Daryl confirmed at no time did Petitioner provide notice of an alleged work injury. (AT 
104,105) After Petitioner stopped working for Clark on October 19th, the company continued to 
pay for his group insurance for approximately 10 months. (AT 106) After Petitioner left Clark, 
Lynn spoke to Petitioner regarding short-term/long-term disability. She spoke to Petitioner 
sometime in  October 2018, before he began receiving short-term disability on October 22, 2018. 
Short-term disability switched to long-term disability on July 29, 2019. Petitioner was paid long-
term disability through March of 2024. He was receiving biweekly checks in the amount of 
$876.00. Short-term and long-term disability payments were provided to all employees of Clark. 
Petitioner continued to work full duty including overtime through October 19, 2018. Between July 
31, 2018 and October 19, 2018, Petitioner's daily job duties were the same, as he worked in 
production, running a mill, banding, packaging. (AT 107-113) 
When Petitioner started working for Clark, he received the company handbook and signed 
off that he read the company handbook with regard to providing notice to his immediate supervisor 
for a work injury. If petitioner reported a work injury, Mr. Tappler would take a statement, and 
26IWCC0128

then report that to plant manager, Joel Stanley. Joel Stanley also advised Lynn that there was no 
work comp claim filed by Petitioner. (AT 114) Lynn testified that there was nothing reduced to 
writing about Petitioner’s alleged incident. Lynn testified “in fact, Mr. Tappler and Joe Stanley 
reported that they never received anything. It would have then came to me then.” (AT 129)  Her 
first notice was receipt of the Application for Adjustment of Claim, one year later. There was no 
report of injury at the time Petitioner was placed on short-term disability. Lynn met with Petitioner 
once. He came into the hallway of the Administration Office and reported that he was going to be 
gone for a while, that he had a degenerative disease and wanted to apply for short-term disability. 
Short-term disability started October 22, 2018. She recalls meeting Petitioner in the hallway, 
Petitioner told Lynn about his illness, and needed to file for short-term disability so that he would 
get compensation. Lynn ran FMLA simultaneously with short-term disability. The only other 
conversation Lynn had with Petitioner was on the phone regarding online rewards. 
 
MEDICAL 
Petitioner was examined by Dr. Jeffrey Coe, on  November 21, 2022 for Petitioner’s 
Independent Medical Examination. Dr. Coe notes that Petitioner reports suffering a work injury 
Himon July 31, 2018. Dr. Coe makes reference to Petitioner’s medical treatment on September 26, 
2018 with Dr. Mark Barba, Ortho Illinois. Dr. Barba references Petitioner’s pain in his hip on and 
off for 13 years. Pain has increased in the last three months, no known injury. Medical report from 
Dr. Van Thiel dated October 15, 2018, provided the same history of pain in the hip on and off for 
13 years. Medical report from Rochelle Community Hospital dated November 5, 2018 indicates 
Petitioner was born with dysplasia and has had difficulties with his hip all of his life, but in the last 
six months, he has had significant increased pain and limited motion making it difficult for him to 
26IWCC0128

walk resulting in surgery being performed on October 31, 2018. Petitioner indicates for several 
years he has been unable to do his hobbies of hunting and fishing, but hopes to get back to doing 
this after rehabilitation. Dr. Coe notes that on August 8, 2019, Petitioner was examined by Dr. 
Ryan Enke  at Ortho Illinois. Dr. Enke references mechanism of injury, gradual onset with no 
known injury but states Petitioner felt something like a pop at his job and has had pain in the groin 
area, right hip and lower back ever since. Dr. Coe’s IME was taken on March 10, 2020. Dr. Coe’s 
evidence deposition was taken on November 21, 2022. Dr. Coe notes that Petitioner had congenital 
pre-existing hip condition of dysplasia, genetically determined and was born with or developed in 
childhood. (P. 48) Dr. Coe testified that Petitioner’s acute injury was significant, it was associated 
with a pop, pain and within a short time seeking medical treatment. Dr. Coe opined it would be a 
significant incident that would be reported to his treating doctors. (P. 51) Dr. Coe testified that 
Petitioner’s treating medical records are inconsistent with what Petitioner told him. Petitioner’s 
treating medical records are consistent with a pre-existing congenital hip dysplasia that references 
right hip pain on and off for 13 years. (P. 56) Medical report from Rochelle Community Hospital 
dated October 17th makes no reference to Petitioner receiving medical treatment for acute injury. 
Medical report dated October 26th makes no mention of an injury. (P. 57)  Report from Dr. Van 
Thiel dated October 31st is consistent with someone receiving treatment for a pre-existing 
congenital hip dysplasia. (P. 59)  Petitioner did not receive any conservative treatment between 
July 31st  and September 26. (P. 60)  Petitioner’s treating medical records from July 31st through 
October 31st do not reference any medical treatment for an accident, or causation for an acute 
work-related injury. (P. 66)  Dr. Coe testified that Petitioner’s pre-existing congenital hip dysplasia 
was a significant factor affecting Petitioner’s ability to perform activities prior to July 31, 2018. 
(P. 68) Dr. Coe agreed that it would be fair to state that there are references in Petitioner’s treating 
26IWCC0128

medical records that show his medical treatment and surgery be causally related to his pre-existing 
medical condition. (P. 85) Dr. Coe testified that after a review of Petitioner’s treating medical 
records through June 30, 2019, Dr. Coe could not testify that Petitioner’s medical treatment was 
related to any kind of accident. (P. 88)  Dr. Coe did not review Petitioner’s actual films, only his 
reports. Dr. Coe found no reference to an acute injury from his review of Petitioner’s diagnostic 
studies. (P. 96) 
Petitioner was examined by Dr. Thangamani on May 1, 2023 at the request of Respondent. 
Petitioner reported to Dr. Thangamani that he was unsure of the exact date of his accident, but 
stated it was on or around July 31, 2018. Questioning Petitioner regarding his pre-existing hip pain 
and his ability to work between the alleged accident date and his first medical evaluation on 
September 26, 2018, Petitioner became upset with the questions and advised that he was not going 
to keep answering questions. After Petitioner was asked additional questions, Petitioner advised 
the visit was over, and Petitioner left the doctor’s office. Dr. Coe notes that the alleged date of 
accident was July 31, 2018, and that Petitioner’s first formal medical treatment was with Dr. Mark 
Barba on September 26, 2018. Petitioner reported to Dr. Barba, right hip pain on and off for 13 
years. Petitioner’s pain has increased in the last three months, with no known injury. Petitioner 
reported to Dr. Thangamani he was unsure how the number 13 years got into his medical records, 
and was also unsure why the medical record stated no known injury. Petitioner also reported to 
Dr. Van Thiel on October 15, 2018, that he has had right hip pain on and off for 13 years, increasing 
over the past three months with no known history. Addressing the issue of causation, Dr. 
Thangamani opined that Petitioner’s current condition of ill-being is due to right hip degenerative 
changes and degenerative labral tearing. Based on the doctor’s review of Petitioner’s treating 
medical records, he cannot link the Petitioner’s current condition and diagnosis to the alleged work 
26IWCC0128

accident of July 31, 2018. He believes Petitioner need for hip surgery is due to previous underlying 
hip issues, with a clearly documented 13-month history of hip pain. Furthermore, per the report of 
the MRI, Petitioner had diffuse labral tearing, which is more consistent with the degenerative 
process. Over time, has hip became more symptomatic, as that is the natural history of significant 
degenerative tearing and impingement. Although Petitioner describes a pop, he is unsure of the 
exact date, there is no documentation to substantiate the report of said injury, and he was able to 
work full duty for several months until obtaining medical treatment. Therefore, it is impossible to 
link his condition of ill-being to an acute injury that occurred on a specific date. With regard to 
Petitioner’s alleged reported accident on July 31, 2018, Dr. Thangamani states Petitioner did return 
to work full duty without restrictions after July 31, 2018, and did not seek medical treatment until 
September 26, 2018, which would lead the doctor to believe that Petitioner did not sustain any 
acute singular work accident that would have required medical restrictions or medical treatment. 
 
The evidence deposition of Dr. Thangamani proceeded on August 31, 2023. The doctor 
testified that while he was  questioning Petitioner regarding any pre-existing hip pain as well as 
his ability to work between the alleged accident date and his first medical evaluation on September 
26, 2018, Petitioner became upset with the doctor. Petitioner advised Dr. Thangamani he was not 
going to keep answering the same questions over and over again. Petitioner advised the doctor the 
visit was over and Dr. Thangamani told Petitioner he was free to leave. (P. 10)  The doctor would 
estimate he was questioning Petitioner about 10 minutes before Petitioner became upset (P. 11,12) 
The doctor was unable to complete his examination due to Petitioner becoming upset and walking 
out of the IME. (P. 12)  The doctor testified hip dysplasia is a broad term that means the hip is not 
shaped properly. Most often, it is caused from just the way you are, just like having flat feet or 
scoliosis or knobby knees, you can have hip dysplasia. You are either born with it or develop it 
26IWCC0128

over time. The doctor noted that both Dr. Barba and Dr. Van Thiel reference in their medical notes 
that Petitioner reported right hip pain on and off for 13 years, increasing over the past three months 
with no known history. The doctor confirmed that his report references Petitioner was unsure of 
the exact date of an incident. There is no documentation to substantiate the report of said injury. 
He was able to work full duty for several months to obtain medical treatment. Therefore, it is 
impossible to link his condition of ill-being to an acute injury that occurred on a specific date. The 
doctor provided a basis of his opinion testifying objectively in reviewing the medical records, it 
appeared that Petitioner had a degenerative condition of the right hip that ultimately led to hip 
replacement. Petitioner’s treating medical records indicate he has had long-standing pain in the 
right hip which is consistent with degenerative changes that the doctor noted on the objective 
findings on imaging. Lastly, Petitioner’s history is inconsistent and that there is not a specific date 
of injury and that Petitioner was able to continue working for several months after time when he 
claims to be injured which is inconsistent with an acute injury that would cause or necessitate hip 
surgery. (P. 20) He reviewed the MRI of the right hip dated January 10, 2019, which revealed 
multifocal degenerative changes to the labrum and right hip joint with osteoarthritic changes. (P. 
23) Dr. Thangamani agreed with the evidence deposition testimony of Dr. Coe wherein Dr. Coe

(P. 30)  Dr. Thangamani agreed with the testimony of Dr. Coe with reference to the medical note 
dated November 5, 2018 from Rochelle Community Hospital, which stated that Petitioner 
indicated for several years he has been unable to do hobbies such as hunting and fishing, but hopes

hip dysplasia, being a significant factor affecting Petitioner’s ability to perform these activities.

(P. 36)  Dr. Thangamani agreed with the testimony of Dr. Coe that based on Dr. Coe’s review of

Dr. Thangamani testified that he agreed with Dr. Coe’s testimony that he could not say that

51-year-old male complains of low back pain. Date of onset and mechanism of injury, July/2018.

CONCLUSIONS OF LAW 
With respect to issue (C) did accident occur that arose out of in the course of Petitioner’s 
employment by Respondent, and with respect to (D), what was the date of accident, the 
Arbitrator finds as follows: 
 
Petitioner testified that on or about July 31, 2018, he was operating mill 315 which is a 
structural cold role formed steel mill. He was working with extremely large heavy studs. While 
working with a large stud that was 50 feet long approximately 400 or 500 pounds, he believes his 
helper inadvertently dropped his end of the heavy stud, causing it to fall causing a shockwave to 
go through Petitioner, wherein Petitioner felt a pop in his right hip. He spoke with Juan Roman, 
who brought Petitioner to see Petitioner's supervisor, Daryl Tappler. Petitioner states he and Daryl 
wrote out a handwritten statement as to what happened. Petitioner submitted Petitioner’s Exhibit 
#4 into evidence with objections made by Respondent with regard to a document titled Clark 
Dietrich Accident Analysis Form. The form references date of accident to be January 19, 2018. 
The Arbitrator notes that the form has no date, is not signed, and that no foundation was laid for 
the report. Petitioner testified that he continued working every day and would go home pretty sore. 
After a while, he noted he was not healing, and therefore scheduled an appointment with Dr. Barba, 
at Ortho Illinois, on September 26, 2018. Dr. Barba’s report dated September 26, 2018 states 
“history per patient: date of onset and mechanism of injury: patient reports of right hip pain on and 
off for 13 years. Pain has increased in the last three months, no known injury.” Petitioner testified 
that when he knew what was happening for sure, he informed Lynn. Lynn told Petitioner to put 
26IWCC0128

his claim under long-term disability. Lynn Ulrich testified that Petitioner stopped working for 
Respondent on October 19, 2018. Around October 22, 2018, Petitioner met with Lynn Ulrich at 
the Administrative Office at Clark Dietrich. Lynn testified that Petitioner reported his medical 
condition was going on for a while and that he had a degenerative disease and asked if he could be 
put on short-term disability. Lynn testified that she agreed, placing Petitioner on FMLA leave, 
simultaneously with short-term disability. This was the only conversation she had with Petitioner 
between July 31st through October 22, 2018. Petitioner testified that after he spoke to Lynn on or 
about October 22, 2018, Lynn instructed Petitioner, he had to put his comp claim under short-term 
disability. He could not submit it under Workmen's Comp. Therefore, he advised his treating 
doctor that he did not know what caused his need for medical treatment. Petitioner testified he told 
his doctor “I didn't know what happened. Basically, I lie to the doctor.” (AT 19) After he spoke to 
Lynn, he did not give a history of anything that happened at work. 
 
Petitioner testified that he was examined by Dr. Jeffrey Coe at the request of his attorneys 
on March 10, 2020. Dr. Coe’s medical report notes Petitioner had congenital pre-existing hip 
condition of dysplasia, genetically determined and was born with this condition or developed it in 
childhood. Petitioner was asked about this reference in Dr. Coe’s IME report. Petitioner testified 
he does not remember Dr. Coe asking him questions about his pre-existing congenital condition. 
He believes Dr. Coe referenced his congenital pre-existing medical condition based off the medical 
report from Dr. Barba’s medical report dated September 26, 2018. Petitioner testified that he was 
diagnosed with a congenital or early developmental anatomic structural abnormality by Dr. Barba 
(AT 39). Dr. Coe testified that Petitioner represented suffering a significant acute injury. It was 
associated with a pop, pain and within a short time seeking medical treatment. Dr. Coe opined it 
would be a significant incident that would be reported to his treating doctors. Dr. Coe testified 
26IWCC0128

Petitioner’s treating medical records are inconsistent with what Petitioner told him. Petitioner’s 
treating medical records are consistent with a pre-existing congenital hip dysplasia that references 
right hip pain on and off for 13 years. Dr. Coe testified that medical records from Rochelle 
Community Hospital failed to reference Petitioner receiving medical treatment for an acute injury. 
Dr. Coe referenced the Dr. Van Thiel’s medical report dated October 31, 2018 is consistent with 
someone receiving treatment for a pre-existing congenital hip dysplasia, rather than an acute 
injury. Dr. Coe testified that Petitioner’s treating medical records prior to March 10, 2020 failed 
to reference Petitioner receiving any medical treatment for an acute work-related injury. Dr. Coe 
testified Petitioner’s pre-existing congenital hip dysplasia was a significant factor affecting his 
ability to perform activities prior to July 31, 2018. Dr. Coe testified that it would be fair to state 
that following his review of Petitioner’s treating medical records, the need for Petitioner’s medical 
treatment and surgeries performed, are causally related to his pre-existing medical condition. 
Petitioner was examined at the request of Respondent by Dr. Thangamani on May 1, 2023. 
Dr. Thangamani’s medical report and testimony confirm that Petitioner walked out of the IME 
after Dr. Thangamani questioned Petitioner regarding Petitioner’s pre-existing hip pain and 
Petitioner’s ability to work between the alleged accident date and first evaluation on September 
26, 2018 with Dr. Barba. Dr. Thangamani’s testimony confirmed that Petitioner’s current 
condition, need for medical treatment and surgery is due to Petitioner’s pre-existing right hip 
degenerative changes and degenerative labral tearing. Based on the doctor’s review of Petitioner’s 
treating medical records, the doctor cannot link Petitioner’s current condition and diagnosis to an 
alleged work injury of July 31, 2018. Petitioner’s need for hip surgeries is due to previous 
underlying hip issues with a clearly documented 13-month history of hip pain. Petitioner's MRI 
report revealed diffuse labral tearing, which is more consistent with the degenerative process. Over 
26IWCC0128

time, Petitioner’s hip became more symptomatic, and that is the natural history of significant 
degenerative tearing and impingement. Dr. Thangamani notes that Petitioner was unsure of the 
exact date of his alleged acute injury, however there is no documentation to substantiate an acute 
injury, and Petitioner was able to work full duty for several months until obtaining treatment on 
September 26, 2018 with Dr. Barba. Therefore, it is impossible to link Petitioner’s condition of ill-
being to an acute injury that occurred on a specific date. 
Petitioner fiancé, Traci Siebler testified that she has  been living with Petitioner for nine 
years. She testified that she attended Petitioner’s medical appointments, and spoke to Petitioner 
regarding his medical appointments. She testified that when Petitioner spoke with his treating 
doctors, he would tell the treating doctors about his work injury. She testified that Petitioner would 
provide his treating doctors with an exact history of what happened when he was working at Clark 
Dietrich. She testified that each and every time Petitioner went  to see his treating doctor, he would 
tell his doctor what his complaints were, any problems he had, and provide his treating doctor with 
a history of what occurred at Clark Dietrich. 
Regarding Petitioner’s alleged accident date of July 31, 2018, the Arbitrator notes that 
Petitioner’s Application for Adjustment of Claim states on or about July 31, 2018. The Arbitrator 
notes that Petitioner first sought medical treatment on September 26, 2018. Medical report from 
Dr. Barba provides a history of present illness, stating the date of onset and mechanism of injury, 
that Petitioner reports right hip pain on and off for 13 years. Pain has increased in the last three 
months, no known injury. The same history was provided to Dr. Van Thiel on October 15, 2018. 
Petitioner testified that he worked for a while every day and would go home sore. Eventually, he 
scheduled an appointment with orthopedic Dr. Barba on September 26, 2018. At such time, Dr. 
Barba states under history of present illness, the date of onset and mechanism of Petitioner’s injury, 
26IWCC0128

that Petitioner reports right hip pain on and off for 13 years. Pain has increased in the last three 
months, no known injury. Petitioner then received treatment on October 15, 2018 with Dr. Van 
Thiel. Again, the history of present illness from Dr. Van Thiel states Petitioner reports of right hip 
pain on and off for 13 years. Petitioner testified that once he knew what was happening, he 
informed Lynn Ulrich, HR business partner at Clark Dietrich. Ms. Ulrich testified that she spoke 
to Petitioner in the Administrative Office hallway of Clark Dietrich on or about October 22, 2018. 
At such time, Petitioner advised Ms. Ulrich that he had an illness and needed to file for short-term 
disability. Petitioner testified that after he spoke to Ms. Ulrich, he lied to his treating doctor, failing 
to provide his treating doctors with a history of accident. The Arbitrator finds no credibility with 
Petitioner’s testimony alleging he began lying to his treating doctors after he spoke to Lynn Ulrich, 
as Petitioner had treatment with Dr. Barba and Dr. Van Thiel prior to his conversation with Lynn 
Ulrich. Petitioner’s testimony is also inconsistent with the testimony of Petitioner’s fiancé, Traci 
Siebler. Ms. Siebler testified that she attended each of Petitioner’s medical appointments with his 
treating doctors. Ms. Siebler testified that at each appointment, Petitioner told the truth to each 
doctor regarding his history of accident. Dr. Coe’s evidence deposition testimony is very clear that 
Petitioner’s treating medical records from September 26, 2018 through the date of Dr. Coe’s IME, 
March 10, 2020, failed to make any reference to an acute injury. Dr. Coe’s testimony was very 
clear that review of Petitioner’s treating medical records are consistent with medical treatment for 
a pre-existing medical condition, rather than an acute injury. Dr. Thangamani’s testimony was very 
clear that Petitioner could not recall the date of his alleged acute injury. Dr. Coe testified that if 
Petitioner had suffered an acute injury, as represented by Petitioner during his examination on May 
10, 2020, the injury would have been significant, and that would have been reported to Petitioner’s 
26IWCC0128

treating doctors. Dr. Coe testified that his review of Petitioner’s treating medical records were 
inconsistent with what Petitioner told him on March 10, 2020. 
For all of the above reasons, after reviewing the entirety of the evidence of record, the 
Arbitrator finds that Petitioner failed to provide any credible evidence that he suffered an  accident  
on July 31, 2018, and failed to provide any evidence that suffered an accident that arose out of and 
in the course of his employment. 
 
With respect to issue (E) was timely notice of the accident given to Respondent, the 
Arbitrator finds as follows: 
 
Petitioner testified that on or about the date of his accident, he met with his supervisor, 
Daryl Tappler. Petitioner testified that Daryl Tappler and Petitioner wrote out a handwritten 
statement as to what happened. Petitioner presented Petitioner’s Exhibit #4, a form titled, Accident 
Analysis from Clark Dietrich. The form referenced date of accident to be January 19, 2018. The 
form is not signed, is not dated, and references date of accident, January 19, 2018. Petitioner 
questioned Lynn Ulrich regarding the form. Ms. Ulrich testified that she personally spoke to Daryl 
Tappler after she was provided notice of Petitioner’s alleged accident, following receipt of 
Petitioner’s Application for Adjustment of Claim. She testified that Daryl Tappler denied any 
knowledge of Petitioner providing alleged notice of a work injury. Ms. Ulrich also testified that 
she again spoke to Petitioner’s supervisor, Daryl Tappler on February 21, 2025, again denying that 
Petitioner provided a notice of an alleged accident. Ms. Ulrich further testified that Daryl Tappler 
provided a statement on July 13, 2019, denying that Petitioner provided any notice of an alleged 
accident. Petitioner testified that he provided notice to Lynn Ulrich on or about October 22, 2018, 
the date he met with Lynn Ulrich in the hallway of the Administration Office at Clark Dietrich. 
Lynn Ulrich denied that Petitioner provided any notice on or about October 22, 2018 of a work 
injury. Instead, Ms. Ulrich testified that Petitioner reported being a degenerative disease/illness, 
26IWCC0128

and that he needed to apply for short-term disability. Ms. Ulrich testified that the first notice she 
was provided that Petitioner was alleging a work injury was receipt of Petitioner’s Application for 
Adjustment of Claim, in September 2019. 
The Arbitrator finds that Petitioner has failed to provide any credible evidence of notice  to 
Respondent. Petitioner testified that he provided notice to supervisor Daryl Tappler and wrote out 
a handwritten statement as to what happened. Petitioner’s trial Exhibit #4 titled, Accident Analysis 
Form from Clark Dietrich states date of accident to be January 19, 2018. Petitioner failed to provide 
any evidence that he provided notice to Daryl Tappler on or about July 31, 2018. Petitioner testified 
that he did not provide notice to Lynn Ulrich until he met with Ms. Ulrich in the hallway of the 
Administration Office at Clark Dietrich on or about October 22, 2018. Ms. Ulrich testified that at 
that  time  Petitioner did not  provide notice of alleged accident on October 22, 2018. The first 
notice she received regarding Petitioner’s alleged accident was receipt of Petitioner’s Application 
for Adjustment of Claim in September 2019. The Arbitrator further notes that Petitioner’s treating 
medical records failed to reference Petitioner suffering an acute injury until Petitioner was 
examined by Petitioner’s IME Dr. Jeffrey Coe on March 10, 2020. The Arbitrator finds that 
Petitioner failed to provide any credible evidence of notice provided to Respondent until 
September 2019, when Respondent received Petitioner’s Application for Adjustment of Claim. 
Wherefore, the Arbitrator denies Petitioner provided statutory notice to Respondent. 
 
 
With respect to the issue (F) is Petitioner’s current condition of ill-being cause related to the 
injury, (J) Were the medical services provided to Petitioner reasonable and necessary? (K) 
What temporary benefits are in dispute, (L) What is a nature and extent of Petitioner’s 
injury, (N) Is Respondent due any credit, the Arbitrator finds as follows: 
 
The Arbitrator has held that Petitioner failed to provide any credible evidence that 
Petitioner suffered an accident that arose out of and in the course of Petitioner’s employment, has 
26IWCC0128

failed to provide any credible evidence to the date of accident, and failed to provide any credible 
evidence that timely notice of accident was provided to respondent. Wherefore, the Arbitrator finds 
that Petitioner’s condition of ill-being and is not causally related to an alleged work injury, medical 
services provided to Petitioner are not causally related to Petitioner’s employment, Petitioner is 
not entitled to any temporary benefits, and the Arbitrator denies the nature and extent of 
Petitioner’s injuries, causally related to a work-related incident. The Arbitrator declines to address 
any credit due Respondent, as Petitioner and Respondent both testified that Petitioner was paid 
short-term and long-term disability benefits through 2024, and Petitioner’s treating medical 
records were paid through group insurance, Marketplace, or through Medicare. The arbitrator finds 
that any inability of the petitioner to continue working after, and need for medical treatment is not 
casually related to any accident arising out of and in the course of his employment with the 
respondent. 
 
For all of the above reasons, and based on the entirety of the evidence of record, 
compensation is hereby denied.
